- `body`: GitHub-flavored markdown in 1–3 short sentences explaining the issue, its impact, and what to change. Reference symbols and file names in backticks. Do not include title/severity headings.
- `location`: `{ "granularity": "line", "file_path": "<final file path>", "start_line": <final right-side line number> }`

Use `granularity: "range"` with `end_line` only when the full finding genuinely spans multiple changed right-side lines. Prefer a single changed line.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". 108	// otherwise block the select loop in waitForLoginURLResult indefinitely, and
109	// with it a sign-in that has already completed. On timeout the goroutine is
110	// abandoned; the CLI is short-lived and exits soon after.
111	func copyLoginURL(copyURL clipboardWriteFunc, loginURL string, timeout time.Duration) error {
112		done := make(chan error, 1)
113		go func() { done <- copyURL(loginURL) }()
114	
115		select {
116		case err := <-done:
117			return err
118		case <-time.After(timeout):
119			return fmt.Errorf("clipboard write timed out after %v", timeout)
120		}
121	}

126	// user from typing. Falls back to the bare verification_uri when the AS
127	// didn't supply a complete form.
128	func chooseApprovalURL(start *auth.DeviceAuthStart) string {
129		if start.VerificationURIComplete != "" {
130			return start.VerificationURIComplete

132		return start.VerificationURI

192	// parseLoginServer validates and canonicalises the --server value: an
193	// http(s) origin with nothing but scheme and host. Userinfo, path, query,
194	// and fragment are rejected rather than silently dropped — the value
195	// becomes the OAuth issuer, the token-exchange target, and the keyring
196	// key, so surprising rewrites would surface as confusing auth failures
197	// much later. A lone trailing slash is tolerated (normalised away).
198	func parseLoginServer(raw string) (string, error) {
199		raw = strings.TrimSpace(raw)
200		if raw == "" {
201			return "", errors.New("empty server URL")
202		}
203		u, err := url.Parse(raw)
204		if err != nil {
205			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse server URL: %w", err)
206		}
207		// Error messages echo u.Redacted(), not raw: the URL may carry
208		// userinfo (that's one of the rejection cases), and stderr often ends
209		// up in CI logs where a password must not appear.
210		switch {
211		case u.Scheme != schemeHTTPS && u.Scheme != schemeHTTP:
212			return "", fmt.Errorf("scheme must be http or https, got %q", u.Redacted())
213		case u.Host == "":
214			return "", fmt.Errorf("missing host in %q", u.Redacted())
215		case u.User != nil:
216			return "", fmt.Errorf("userinfo not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
217		case u.Path != "" && u.Path != "/":
218			return "", fmt.Errorf("path not allowed in %q (use the bare origin)", u.Redacted())
219		case u.RawQuery != "" || u.Fragment != "":
220			return "", fmt.Errorf("query/fragment not allowed in %q", u.Redacted())
221		}
222		return api.NormalizeOriginURL(raw), nil
223	}

225	// requireSecureLoginServer enforces TLS for the chosen login server — the
226	// only host login dials. --insecure-http-auth opts in to http:// (and
227	// enables it process-wide for the token save path).
228	func requireSecureLoginServer(server string, insecureHTTPAuth bool) error {
229		if insecureHTTPAuth {
230			auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()
231			return nil
232		}
233		if err := api.RequireSecureURL(server); err != nil {
234			return fmt.Errorf("login server check: %w", err)
235		}
236		return nil
237	}

239	func runLogin(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, client deviceAuthClient, urlInteractor loginURLInteractor, canPrompt bool) error {
240		start, err := client.StartDeviceAuth(ctx)
241		if err != nil {
242			return fmt.Errorf("start login: %w", err)
243		}
244	
245		approvalURL := chooseApprovalURL(start)
246		fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Device code: %s\n", start.UserCode)
247		printLoginURL(outW, deviceLoginURLLabel, approvalURL)
248	
249		wait := func(waitCtx context.Context) (loginTokens, error) {
250			accessToken, refreshToken, waitErr := waitForApproval(
251				waitCtx,
252				client,
253				start.DeviceCode,
254				start.ExpiresIn,
255				time.Duration(start.Interval)*time.Second,
256				defaultSlowDownBackoff,
257			)
258			return loginTokens{accessToken: accessToken, refreshToken: refreshToken}, waitErr
259		}
260	
261		var result loginTokens
262		if canPrompt {
263			result, err = waitForLoginURLResult(ctx, outW, errW, approvalURL, "Waiting for approval… ", urlInteractor, wait)
264		} else {
265			fmt.Fprint(outW, "Waiting for approval… ")
266			result, err = wait(ctx)
267		}
268		if err != nil {
269			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
270		}
271	
272		return persistLogin(outW, client.BaseURL(), result.accessToken, result.refreshToken)
273	}

280	// loginFlowFacts carries the environment facts that pick between the
281	// browser and device-code flows. Detection happens once at the command
282	// entry point; the decision logic below only consumes these values.
283	type loginFlowFacts struct {
284		useDevice  bool // --device flag
285		canPrompt  bool // interactive terminal present
286		sshSession bool // running inside an SSH session
287	}
288	
289	// runLoginAuto picks between the browser (loopback authorization-code) and
290	// device-code flows and runs the chosen one. The browser flow is the
291	// default — no code to type, no poll latency — but it needs a browser that
292	// can reach this machine's 127.0.0.1, so headless terminals (CI, piped
293	// stdin), SSH sessions, and a loopback listener that fails to start all
294	// fall back to the device flow with a one-line explanation; the same
295	// both-flows-with-fallback shape gh / gcloud / aws sso ship. --device
296	// forces the device flow without commentary.
297	func runLoginAuto(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, deviceClient deviceAuthClient, startBrowser func(context.Context) (browserAuthFlow, error), urlInteractor loginURLInteractor, facts loginFlowFacts) error {
298		if shouldUseBrowserLogin(facts) {
299			flow, err := startBrowser(ctx)
300			if err != nil {
301				// Binding the loopback listener can fail (sandboxing, firewall,
302				// exhausted ports); that shouldn't strand the user — warn and
303				// use the device flow instead.
304				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: could not start browser sign-in (%v); falling back to the device-code flow.\n", err)
305				return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, urlInteractor, facts.canPrompt)
306			}
307			return runBrowserLogin(ctx, outW, errW, flow, deviceClient.BaseURL(), urlInteractor, browserLoginTimeout)
308		}
309		switch {
310		case facts.useDevice:
311			// Explicitly requested; no explanation needed.
312		case !facts.canPrompt:
313			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "No interactive terminal detected; using device-code flow.")
314		case facts.sshSession:
315			fmt.Fprintln(errW, "SSH session detected; using device-code flow (a browser opened here couldn't reach this machine).")
316		}
317		return runLogin(ctx, outW, errW, deviceClient, urlInteractor, facts.canPrompt)
318	}

320	// shouldUseBrowserLogin reports whether `entire login` should use the
321	// loopback authorization-code (browser) flow. The browser flow is the
322	// default but needs a local browser + reachable 127.0.0.1, so it's only
323	// chosen when --device wasn't passed, an interactive terminal is present,
324	// and we're not inside an SSH session (where the loopback listener binds
325	// on the remote host, out of the user's browser's reach); otherwise the
326	// caller falls back to the device flow.
327	func shouldUseBrowserLogin(f loginFlowFacts) bool {
328		return !f.useDevice && f.canPrompt && !f.sshSession
329	}

331	// isSSHSession reports whether this process is running inside an SSH
332	// session: sshd sets SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT for every session and
333	// SSH_TTY for interactive ones.
334	func isSSHSession() bool {
335		return os.Getenv("SSH_CONNECTION") != "" ||
336			os.Getenv("SSH_CLIENT") != "" ||
337			os.Getenv("SSH_TTY") != ""

340	// runBrowserLogin runs the loopback authorization-code flow on an
341	// already-started flow: show the authorization URL and explicit actions, wait
342	// up to waitTimeout for the redirect back to the local listener, then exchange
343	// the code for tokens. Shares the token validation + persistence tail with
344	// runLogin via persistLogin.
345	func runBrowserLogin(ctx context.Context, outW, errW io.Writer, flow browserAuthFlow, baseURL string, urlInteractor loginURLInteractor, waitTimeout time.Duration) error {
346		// Wait tears the listener down on return, but Close is idempotent and
347		// covers the error paths before Wait runs.
348		defer func() { _ = flow.Close() }()
349	
350		authURL := flow.AuthorizationURL()
351		fmt.Fprintf(outW, "Logging in to %s\n\n", baseURL)
352		printLoginURL(outW, browserLoginURLLabel, authURL)
353	
354		// Start the deadline as soon as the URL is visible. Waiting for the
355		// loopback redirect and reading URL actions then proceed concurrently, so
356		// clicking or pasting the URL can complete login without a terminal key.
357		waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, waitTimeout)
358		defer cancel()
359	
360		code, err := waitForLoginURLResult(
361			waitCtx,
362			outW,
363			errW,
364			authURL,
365			"Waiting for sign-in… ",
366			urlInteractor,
367			flow.Wait,
368		)
369		if err != nil {
370			if errors.Is(waitCtx.Err(), context.DeadlineExceeded) {
371				return fmt.Errorf("timed out waiting for sign-in after %v; run `entire login` again, or use `entire login --device`", waitTimeout)
372			}
373			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
374		}
375	
376		token, refreshToken, err := flow.Exchange(ctx, code)
377		if err != nil {
378			return fmt.Errorf("complete login: %w", err)
379		}
380	
381		return persistLogin(outW, baseURL, token, refreshToken)
382	}

384	// persistLogin validates the freshly-issued access token and records it in
385	// the shared contexts.json credential model. Shared by the device-code and
386	// browser flows.
387	func persistLogin(outW io.Writer, baseURL, token, refreshToken string) error {
388		if err := validateReceivedToken(token, baseURL, time.Now()); err != nil {
389			return fmt.Errorf("reject login token: %w", err)
390		}
391	
392		// Record the login in the shared contexts.json credential model — the
393		// single store every consumer (control plane, data API, git remote
394		// helper, entiredb's CLIs) resolves against.
395		if _, err := auth.RecordLoginContext(token, refreshToken, true); err != nil {
396			return fmt.Errorf("save login: %w", withHeadlessStoreHint(err))
397		}
398	
399		fmt.Fprintln(outW, "✓ Login complete.")
400		return nil
401	}
402	
403	// withHeadlessStoreHint appends file-token-store guidance to a credential
404	// store write failure. The default backend is the OS keyring, which locked
405	// or keyring-less machines (CI, containers, minimal server VMs) can't use —
406	// the raw store error gives those users no way forward (#1036). The hint is
407	// skipped when ENTIRE_TOKEN_STORE=file is already set (suggesting it again
408	// would be nonsense) and for failures the file store wouldn't help with.
409	func withHeadlessStoreHint(err error) error {
410		if !errors.Is(err, auth.ErrCredentialStoreWrite) || tokenstore.FileBackendSelected() {
411			return err
412		}
413	
414		return fmt.Errorf("%w\n\nIf this machine has no usable OS keyring (headless server, container, CI), store tokens in a file instead:\n\n  %s=file entire login\n\nTokens are then written with 0600 permissions to %s (override the location with %s)",
415			err, tokenstore.BackendEnvVar, tokenstore.FileBackendPath(), tokenstore.PathEnvVar)
416	}

418	// validateReceivedToken runs minimum-trust checks on the access token
419	// the AS handed us before we persist it. The server is the authority
420	// on signature/exp; this is defense in depth aimed at catching gross
421	// misbehaviour by a compromised or misconfigured AS (e.g. handing back
422	// a token from a different issuer than the one we asked, or one whose
423	// claims are already-expired).
424	//
425	// It also enforces what the contexts model needs up front:
426	// RecordLoginContext — the sole persistence path — keys the context and
427	// keychain slot on the token's iss and handle/sub claims, so a token
428	// without parseable claims can never complete a login. Rejecting it here
429	// names the requirement instead of surfacing a parse error from the save
430	// step. Entire-core always issues claim-bearing JWTs; opaque-token-only
431	// servers are not supported.
432	func validateReceivedToken(rawToken, issuerURL string, now time.Time) error {
433		claims, err := tokens.ParseClaims(rawToken)
434		if errors.Is(err, tokens.ErrUnsignedJWT) {
435			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // sentinel surfaces verbatim for caller's errors.Is
436		}
437		if err != nil {
438			return fmt.Errorf("login server issued a token without parseable JWT claims (claim-bearing JWTs are required): %w", err)
439		}
440		if claims.Issuer == "" {
441			return errors.New("token has no iss claim; cannot record a login context")
442		}
443		if claims.Handle == "" && claims.Subject == "" {
444			return errors.New("token has no handle or sub claim; cannot record a login context")
445		}
446	
447		// iss check: the token must claim to come from the issuer we sent
448		// the device-code request to. A mismatch means either the AS is
449		// misconfigured or someone's playing games.
450		if issErr := issMatches(claims.Issuer, issuerURL); issErr != nil {
451			return issErr
452		}
453	
454		// exp sanity: a token that's already expired before we even store
455		// it is a smell. Don't reject if exp is unset (some servers omit).
456		if !claims.ExpiresAt.IsZero() && !now.Before(claims.ExpiresAt) {
457			return fmt.Errorf("token already expired (exp=%s, now=%s)",
458				claims.ExpiresAt.Format(time.RFC3339), now.Format(time.RFC3339))
459		}
460	
461		return nil
462	}
463	
464	// issMatches reports whether claimed equals expected after stripping path/
465	// query/fragment via api.OriginOnly, so "https://issuer/" and "https://issuer"
466	// match. The caller has already rejected an empty iss claim.
467	func issMatches(claimed, expected string) error {
468		normClaimed := api.OriginOnly(claimed)
469		normExpected := api.OriginOnly(expected)
470		if normClaimed != normExpected {
471			return fmt.Errorf("iss mismatch: token claims %q, expected %q", normClaimed, normExpected)
472		}
473		return nil
474	}

476	func waitForApproval(ctx context.Context, poller deviceAuthClient, deviceCode string, expiresIn int, interval, slowDownBackoff time.Duration) (accessToken, refreshToken string, err error) {
477		expiry := time.Duration(expiresIn) * time.Second
478		if expiry <= 0 || expiry > maxExpiresIn {
479			expiry = maxExpiresIn
480		}
481		deadline := time.Now().Add(expiry)
482		pollInterval := interval
483		if pollInterval <= 0 {
484			pollInterval = fallbackDeviceAuthPollInterval
485		}
486	
487		consecutiveErrors := 0
488	
489		for {
490			if time.Now().After(deadline) {
491				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")
492			}
493	
494			result, err := poller.PollDeviceAuth(ctx, deviceCode)
495			if err != nil {
496				consecutiveErrors++
497				if consecutiveErrors >= maxTransientErrors {
498					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("poll approval status (after %d consecutive failures): %w", consecutiveErrors, err)
499				}
500				// Transient error — wait and retry.
501				select {
502				case <-ctx.Done():
503					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("wait for approval: %w", ctx.Err())
504				case <-time.After(pollInterval):
505				}
506				continue
507			}
508			consecutiveErrors = 0
509	
510			switch result.Error {
511			case "":
512				if result.AccessToken == "" {
513					return "", "", errors.New("device authorization completed without a token")
514				}
515				return result.AccessToken, result.RefreshToken, nil
516			case "authorization_pending":
517				// no-op, will sleep and retry below
518			case "slow_down":
519				pollInterval += slowDownBackoff
520				if pollInterval > maxPollInterval {
521					pollInterval = maxPollInterval
522				}
523			case "access_denied":
524				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization denied")
525			case "expired_token":
526				return "", "", errors.New("device authorization expired")
527			default:
528				if result.ErrorDescription != "" {
529					return "", "", fmt.Errorf("device authorization failed: %s: %s", result.Error, result.ErrorDescription)
530				}
531				return "", "", fmt.Errorf("device authorization failed: %s", result.Error)
532			}
533	
534			select {
535			case <-ctx.Done():
536				return "", "", fmt.Errorf("wait for approval: %w", ctx.Err())
537			case <-time.After(pollInterval):
538			}
539		}
540	}

569	type loginURLActionResult struct {
570		action loginURLAction
571		err    error
572	}
573	
574	type loginURLWaitResult[T any] struct {
575		value T
576		err   error
577	}
578	
579	// waitForLoginURLResult runs authentication and terminal input concurrently.
580	// A completed authentication cancels and joins the input reader before
581	// returning, which guarantees Bubble Tea restores the terminal from raw mode.
582	// Copy leaves both actions available; a successful browser open stops reading
583	// keys and waits only for authentication to finish.
584	func waitForLoginURLResult[T any](
585		ctx context.Context,
586		outW, errW io.Writer,
587		loginURL, waitingMessage string,
588		interactor loginURLInteractor,
589		wait func(context.Context) (T, error),
590	) (T, error) {
591		flowCtx, cancelFlow := context.WithCancel(ctx)
592		defer cancelFlow()
593	
594		actionCtx, cancelAction := context.WithCancel(flowCtx)
595		defer cancelAction()
596	
597		waitCh := make(chan loginURLWaitResult[T], 1)
598		go func() {
599			value, err := wait(flowCtx)
600			waitCh <- loginURLWaitResult[T]{value: value, err: err}
601		}()
602	
603		actionCh := make(chan loginURLActionResult, 1)
604		actionActive := false
605		startActionRead := func() {
606			actionActive = true
607			go func() {
608				action, err := interactor.readAction(actionCtx)
609				actionCh <- loginURLActionResult{action: action, err: err}
610			}()
611		}
612		finishActionRead := func() {
613			cancelAction()
614			if actionActive {
615				<-actionCh
616				actionActive = false
617			}
618		}
619	
620		statusLineOpen := false
621		renderInitialPrompt := func() {
622			// Only advertise the keys when the terminal can actually deliver them.
623			// Authentication still completes through the always-visible URL.
624			if interactor.keysAvailable() {
625				fmt.Fprintln(outW, loginURLPrompt)
626			}
627			fmt.Fprint(outW, waitingMessage)
628			statusLineOpen = true
629		}
630		finishStatusLine := func() {
631			if statusLineOpen {
632				fmt.Fprintln(outW)
633				statusLineOpen = false
634			}
635		}
636		renderInitialPrompt()
637		startActionRead()
638	
639		for {
640			select {
641			case result := <-waitCh:
642				finishActionRead()
643				finishStatusLine()
644				return result.value, result.err
645			case result := <-actionCh:
646				actionActive = false
647				finishStatusLine()
648	
649				// Authentication may have completed at the same time as the key
650				// arrived. Prefer that result over launching a stale side effect.
651				select {
652				case waitResult := <-waitCh:
653					cancelAction()
654					return waitResult.value, waitResult.err
655				default:
656				}
657	
658				if result.err != nil {
659					cancelFlow()
660					<-waitCh
661					var zero T
662					return zero, result.err
663				}
664	
665				switch result.action {
666				case loginURLNone:
667					// A controlling TTY disappeared between prompt detection and
668					// use (or tests disabled real terminal input). Authentication
669					// still runs and can complete through the visible URL.
670					cancelAction()
671					result := <-waitCh
672					return result.value, result.err
673				case loginURLCopy:
674					if err := copyLoginURL(interactor.copyURL, loginURL, clipboardCopyTimeout); err != nil {
675						fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to copy login URL: %v\n", err)
676					} else {
677						fmt.Fprintln(outW, "✓ Copied to clipboard.")
678					}
679					startActionRead()
680				case loginURLOpen:
681					if err := interactor.openURL(flowCtx, loginURL); err != nil {
682						fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: failed to open default browser: %v\n", err)
683						startActionRead()
684						continue
685					}
686	
687					cancelAction()
688					fmt.Fprintln(outW, "✓ Opened browser.")
689					result := <-waitCh

The search results show discussions around error handling in Bubble Tea, particularly regarding how `tea.Program.Run()` handles errors. tea.Quit simply stops tea.Program.Run execution, and AFAIK, you can't control what error being returned from tea.Program.Run aside from OS related problems.

There are also issues related to stdin handling in Bubble Tea. When using WithInput(nil), one issue is that any keys typed appear in the terminal and ctrl+c exits, rather than properly disabling input as expected.

Regarding EOF on stdin specifically, the search results discuss that Bubble Tea apps assume control of stdin and stdout, which means stdin EOF conditions may cause unexpected behavior or errors when the program encounters an end-of-file on standard input.

If you're experiencing a specific error when stdin reaches EOF, it's likely related to how Bubble Tea handles terminal input when there's no more data available. The framework expects interactive input and may not gracefully handle stdin EOF in all cases. You might need to use `WithInput()` option to provide a specific input source or handle EOF conditions in your model's Update method.
